tasks.title: Freeze the portable artifact contracts
tasks.details: Publish versioned JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) contracts and domain invariants. MVP_SPEC.md controls scope; research documents provide historical context. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 3-5, 7-11, 14; AGENTS.md sections 2-5.
steps: Specify schemas for definitions, cases, assessments, calibration plans, profiles, run reports, evaluations, and comparisons.
Define JSON Lines (JSONL) records, dataset metadata, version compatibility, immutable values, and stable reason codes.
Separate invalid input, execution failure, uncertain judgment, rejection, completion status, qualification, and application authorization.
Specify public operation inputs, outputs, modes, resource limits, and failure behavior.
Record TypeScript-first delivery and the later Python delivery; retain the current list of deferred features.
Specify how exact-only runs satisfy profile compatibility without statistical calibration.

tasks.title: Publish the supported input schema subset
tasks.details: Define the portable JSON Schema 2020-12 subset before selecting validation dependencies. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4-5, 14-15.
steps: List supported keywords for strings, finite numbers, booleans, arrays, and objects.
Require an object at the input root, all top-level properties, and additionalProperties: false.
Specify nested required properties, unsupported features, numeric bounds, nesting limits, and input size limits.
Document permitted TypeBox metadata removal without dropping validation constraints.
Define field-path errors and disable coercion, mutation, implicit input defaults, and external schema retrieval.

tasks.title: Specify canonical hashes and string semantics
tasks.details: Use one Rust procedure for canonicalization, content hashes, string length, and matching. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4-5, 8-10, 15.
steps: Define numeric limits, numeric representation, omitted values, object keys, Unicode handling, and ordered arrays.
Define hash domains and content boundaries for definitions, inputs, translations, profiles, plans, datasets, and splits.
Specify maxLength counting and includes/excludes matching, including empty strings and Unicode edge cases.
Specify profile self-hash handling and the treatment of nonportable JavaScript values.
Document which changes alter identity and why a hash does not establish stochastic replay.

tasks.title: Bootstrap Rust and TypeScript workspaces
tasks.details: Create the shared Rust library and the TypeScript software development kit (SDK). Keep the public application programming interface (API) independent of providers. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 14; AGENTS.md sections 2, 5-6.
steps: Create the Rust core, thin NAPI-RS binding, and one public TypeScript package with a command-line interface (CLI).
Declare supported Node versions and operating system, architecture, and runtime targets.
Pin necessary dependencies after checking schema support, numerical needs, and target compatibility.
Add Apache-2.0 licensing, package metadata, development commands, and generated-file exclusions.
Keep provider calls, credentials, storage, and rendering outside the Rust core.

tasks.title: Add deterministic verification automation
tasks.details: Establish repeatable checks before behavior implementation. Ordinary checks must need no credentials or paid API calls. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 15; AGENTS.md sections 6-8, 11.
steps: Configure Rust tests, formatting, linting, TypeScript checks, and Vitest.
Add schema, example, documentation-link, and project-name checks.
Configure continuous integration for the declared initial targets.
Provide deterministic clocks, identifiers, randomness, and fake external boundaries for tests.
Document the red, green, refactor workflow and separate opt-in live evaluations.

tasks.title: Create shared contract conformance fixtures
tasks.details: Publish language-neutral valid and invalid fixtures before wrappers diverge. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4-5, 15; AGENTS.md section 6.
steps: Cover each definition shape, input type, outcome, profile state, and invalid contract invariant.
Provide equivalent TypeBox and JSON definitions with expected canonical content and hashes.
Include ordered scales, Unicode, numeric boundaries, serialization round trips, and rejected executable values.
Define runtime traces for queue limits, deadlines, cancellation, retries, partial failure, and late results.
Make these fixtures mandatory for the later Python wrapper.

tasks.title: Model execution transitions with TLA+
tasks.details: Use Temporal Logic of Actions (TLA+) before implementing critical execution state. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 12; AGENTS.md section 7; research/05-formal-verification-extension.md section 8.
steps: Define bounded queue, active attempt, retry, cancellation, completion, and late-result transitions.
Check that active execution never exceeds its limit and terminal reports cannot change.
Check that retries preserve the case input and profile binding.
Check that errors and skipped work cannot become passes.
Record TLC version, configuration, bounds, assumptions, completion status, and required fairness.
Specify the mapping to Rust state validation and wrapper scheduling, including omitted behavior.

tasks.title: Model profile qualification and host selection
tasks.details: Model qualification separately from trusted host selection and application actions. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8-10; AGENTS.md section 7.
steps: Define candidate, qualification, evaluation, shadow, host selection, and enforcement transitions.
Check that incompatible or unvalidated profiles cannot enter enforcement.
Check that running or evaluating a profile cannot promote it.
Check that shadow outcomes cannot authorize application actions.
Record checked bounds, tool versions, assumptions, completion status, and implementation mapping.
Retain counterexamples as applicable regression scenarios without weakening invariants.

tasks.title: Implement strict Rust contract parsing
tasks.details: Make Rust the authoritative validation boundary for external artifacts. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4-5, 8, 10, 12; AGENTS.md sections 4, 10.
steps: Write failing fixtures for malformed artifacts, invalid versions, invalid field types, and contract violations.
Implement serializable domain types and schema validation for the frozen artifact contracts.
Return stable typed errors with field paths and sanitized causes.
Enforce contract size and nesting bounds without coercion or silent defaults.
Reject unsupported data before exposing validated domain values.

tasks.title: Validate portable definitions and input schemas
tasks.details: Enforce check meaning independently of evaluator behavior. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 4; AGENTS.md section 4.
steps: Test duplicate IDs, empty check sets, missing names, and invalid or empty using lists.
Require exactly one question or rule and exactly one answer map or ordered scale for questions.
Validate labels, disjoint accept/review selections, ordered scale levels, and accept.at_least.
Recognize binary questions only when the answer keys are exactly yes and no.
Default omitted when_uncertain to review and reject other uncertainty behavior.
Validate the supported object schema and reject every unsupported constraint.

tasks.title: Validate cases and project authorized inputs
tasks.details: Validate complete cases before execution and expose only each check's declared inputs. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4-6, 10, 12.
steps: Write failing tests for missing fields, extra fields, wrong types, oversized inputs, and invalid case identifiers.
Validate input data in Rust using the frozen schema subset.
Project each check's input from its using list without modifying the original case.
Keep labels, explanations, baseline decisions, and unrelated metadata outside evaluator requests.
Return explicit validation failures before any provider call.

tasks.title: Implement canonical content hashes in Rust
tasks.details: Use the specified canonicalization for all artifact identities. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4-5, 8-10, 15.
steps: Write shared hash fixtures before implementing the canonicalizer.
Implement canonical content and hashes for definitions, inputs, translations, profiles, plans, datasets, and splits.
Preserve scale and other ordered-array positions.
Test object-order invariance, numeric boundaries, Unicode, and rejection of nonportable values.
Verify serialization round trips and profile self-hash validation.

tasks.title: Implement the exact string rules
tasks.details: Implement maxLength, includes, and excludes on one string input. Exact rules need no statistical calibration. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4-5.
steps: Write boundary tests for each rule using the specified Unicode length and matching semantics.
Reject invalid rule parameters and invalid input projections.
Implement deterministic rule assessment in Rust.
Return pass or fail with the executed rule and a useful reason.
Verify that no provider, numerical confidence, or calibration evidence is required.

tasks.title: Implement outcomes and immutable report records
tasks.details: Separate component outcomes, aggregate outcome, and execution completion. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 9-10; AGENTS.md sections 4, 10.
steps: Write table-driven tests for pass, fail, review, error, and skipped combinations.
Aggregate fail first, then error, then review or skipped, then pass.
Preserve all component outcomes, including errors when another check fails.
Record stable IDs, content hashes, assessments, applied rules, evaluator versions, timing, usage, and sanitized reasons.
Keep evidence references distinct from evaluator-returned support.
Make completed records immutable and exclude application authorization.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic run state transitions
tasks.details: Apply the checked execution model at the Rust boundary. The wrapper remains responsible for scheduling. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 5; AGENTS.md section 7.
steps: Turn model transitions and relevant counterexamples into failing regression tests.
Validate attempt, result, cancellation, and terminal transitions in Rust.
Reject late, duplicate, or mismatched results that could change terminal state.
Bind attempts to the same case and profile identities.
Preserve cancellation and completion status independently of aggregate outcome.
Map each implemented transition to the checked TLA+ model.

tasks.title: Expose the core through a thin NAPI-RS binding
tasks.details: Expose serializable Rust operations without leaking native types into the TypeScript API. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 5.
steps: Write native-boundary tests for valid requests and malformed data.
Expose validation, projection, hashing, exact rules, report construction, and state validation.
Translate Rust failures into stable TypeScript errors without losing safe causes.
Preserve numeric and string behavior across the native boundary.
Verify that loading the binding performs no provider calls or application storage.

tasks.title: Implement TypeBox defineChecks authoring
tasks.details: Return validated, serializable definitions with inferred case inputs and using names. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4-5, 15.
steps: Write type tests for inferred inputs and unknown names in using.
Convert supported TypeBox object schemas into the portable contract.
Reject callbacks, closures, transforms, custom validators, and JavaScript-only values before serialization loses them.
Remove only documented authoring metadata and preserve all supported constraints.
Use Rust validation and shared hash fixtures for TypeBox and equivalent JSON.
Expose public types without provider SDK or native binding types.

tasks.title: Implement load and the exact-rule run path
tasks.details: Support trusted imported definitions and explicit JSON paths without intermediate exports in the normal library workflow. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 9, 11.
steps: Write an integration test that loads a typed definition, validates a case, and returns an exact-rule report.
Implement load for validated definitions and explicitly supplied JSON files.
Implement run through Rust projection, exact rules, state validation, and report construction.
Inject file access, clocks, and identifiers at the wrapper boundary.
Reject YAML and TypeScript source loading through data-file paths.
Preserve host ownership of credentials, storage, permissions, and business actions.

tasks.title: Verify the exact-rule vertical slice
tasks.details: Establish the first complete Rust-to-TypeScript path before adding semantic execution. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 14-15.
steps: Run identical cases through TypeBox authoring and exported JSON.
Verify equal canonical content, hashes, rule outcomes, and serialized reports.
Exercise malformed native requests, invalid cases, Unicode boundaries, and all exact rule types.
Confirm that the slice works without credentials, network calls, or provider packages.
Document one reproducible smoke command and its expected observable result.

tasks.title: Build prebuilt Node packages
tasks.details: Package native artifacts for the declared Node platform matrix before expanding the API. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 14-15.
steps: Build the NAPI-RS artifacts for every declared supported target.
Package the TypeScript entry points, declarations, schemas, and required native artifact selection.
Ensure supported installations need no Rust compiler.
Return a clear installation or loading error on unsupported targets.
Verify package contents, license files, version consistency, and excluded private or generated artifacts.

tasks.title: Verify clean Node installations
tasks.details: Make successful native installation an early delivery gate. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 14-15.
steps: Install packed artifacts in clean environments for each declared Node target.
Remove Rust tooling from the installation environment.
Run the exact-rule smoke case through public imports.
Check supported module formats, type declarations, and native artifact resolution.
Record supported targets and require these checks in continuous integration.

tasks.title: Implement evaluator registration and execution contracts
tasks.details: Receive validated questions, projected inputs, budgets, and cancellation signals through a small portable interface. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5-6, 12.
steps: Write contract tests for typed assessments and operational errors.
Implement explicit host registration with stable evaluator and adapter identities.
Reject unknown evaluator references without installing plugins or executing code.
Preserve label-only outputs and absent optional measurements.
Keep network access, credentials, and provider SDK types outside the Rust core and public definitions.

tasks.title: Add test evaluators and adapter conformance cases
tasks.details: Use fake and label-only adapters to demonstrate independence from Jev response shapes. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 6, 14-15.
steps: Implement deterministic test adapters with success, review, malformed response, error, and delayed response controls.
Verify that missing confidence, distributions, usage, and evidence references remain absent.
Exercise a separately specified test decision rule for label-only assessments.
Keep check meaning unchanged when replacing the evaluator.
Require an independent profile binding when evaluator behavior changes.
Publish reusable adapter conformance cases for the future Python wrapper.

tasks.title: Verify and pin the official Jev SDK contract
tasks.details: Confirm current provider contracts when implementation begins. The existing specification records design-time assumptions. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5-6 and References.
steps: Check official @typesafe-ai/sdk documentation for Choice, Noul, Score, cancellation, retries, and batching.
Record model version resolution, response shapes, service limits, and supported usage fields.
Pin a compatible SDK version and document the supported model configuration.
Create sanitized provider fixtures with provenance and clearly identified synthetic examples.
Identify unavailable metadata and define explicit handling without invented values.

tasks.title: Translate checks into versioned Jev questions
tasks.details: Translate named answers to Choice, explicit yes/no answers to Noul, and ordered scales to Score. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4, 6, 12.
steps: Write translation fixtures for categorical, binary, and ordered questions.
Preserve question wording, answer descriptions, scale order, and exact projected input fields.
Frame supplied content as evidence and exclude labels, label explanations, and baseline decisions.
Record complete translated questions, adapter versions, and canonical translation hashes.
Verify that changed translation behavior changes the evaluator binding.

tasks.title: Normalize Jev assessments and execution failures
tasks.details: Preserve actual provider measurements and distinguish operational failures from semantic outcomes. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 6, 9, 12.
steps: Test real response shapes with sanitized fixtures and synthetic malformed variants.
Normalize labels, Noul values, Score positions, distributions, optional confidence, and supported evidence references.
Validate normalized assessments in Rust, including labels, ranges, distribution structure, and input-bound reference validity.
Keep Noul confidence absent and preserve fractional Score values without rounding.
Map timeouts, provider errors, invalid responses, usage, timing, and actual model versions into typed records.
Sanitize provider error text without hiding the operational reason.

tasks.title: Implement Jev decision policies in Rust
tasks.details: Apply the v0 abstention policy to provider measurements without claiming calibrated correctness probabilities. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 6.
steps: Write table-driven tests for acceptance and rejection cutoffs, boundary equality, and review outcomes.
Calculate acceptable and unacceptable mass from Choice distributions, Noul values, and ordered Score distributions.
Require both cutoffs to exceed 0.5 and reject invalid policy parameters.
Keep explicitly review-labeled Choice answers as review.
Apply recorded Choice/Score confidence floors only when supported and required by the selected policy.
Verify that Score means cannot substitute for distribution mass and missing required measurements fail explicitly.

tasks.title: Validate profiles and evaluator compatibility
tasks.details: Bind immutable profiles to exact definitions, evaluators, policies, and declared scope. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8, 12, 15.
steps: Write mismatch tests for definitions, schemas, projections, preprocessing, models, adapters, translations, policies, and scope.
Validate profile schema versions, IDs, content hashes, qualification states, and required evidence references.
Compare resolved model versions before accepting enforcement bindings.
Reject material mismatches before evaluator execution.
Keep credentials and raw private case content outside profiles.
Explain that content consistency cannot authenticate labels, population claims, or host approval.

tasks.title: Generate explicit exploration profiles
tasks.details: Let developers try semantic checks before collecting qualification evidence. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8, 11, 14.
steps: Generate a versioned starter profile from validated definitions and registered evaluator bindings.
Record starter numerical parameters and effective execution configuration.
Mark the profile unvalidated and explain that starter thresholds have no qualification evidence.
Permit evaluation and shadow use while rejecting enforcement.
Test that executing the profile never changes its qualification.

tasks.title: Implement bounded scheduling and saturation records
tasks.details: The TypeScript wrapper owns queues and concurrency. Saturated work returns explicit skipped records. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 9, 12.
steps: Write deterministic tests for active work limits, pending work limits, and simultaneous submissions.
Implement explicit scheduler bounds from the effective execution configuration.
Produce skipped records with stable reasons when the queue cannot accept work.
Attempt every required check unless an operational limit prevents execution.
Prevent semantic failures from triggering cost-based short-circuiting.
Feed state transitions through Rust validation and release resources on terminal paths.

tasks.title: Enforce total deadlines and cancellation
tasks.details: Deadlines cover queue time, attempts, and backoff. Terminal reports cannot accept late changes. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 12.
steps: Write controlled-clock tests for queued, active, and partially completed cancellation.
Apply one total execution deadline across the complete attempt lifecycle.
Propagate cancellation to adapters and clean up queued and active work.
Record timeouts as operational errors and retain completed component results.
Reject late results after cancellation, deadline completion, or normal completion.
Verify that adapters which ignore cancellation cannot mutate terminal reports.

tasks.title: Implement bounded retries without binding drift
tasks.details: Configure retries once and keep each attempt within its original run budget and bindings. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 12; AGENTS.md section 7.
steps: Write tests for retryable failures, permanent failures, exhausted attempts, and cancellation during backoff.
Define retryable operational reason codes and bounded backoff behavior.
Configure SDK and wrapper retries to prevent multiplied attempts.
Reuse the same case input, projected state, profile, translation, and resolved model binding.
Include retries and backoff within the total deadline.
Record attempts and final failure without converting execution errors into semantic answers.

tasks.title: Enforce provider input limits and call isolation
tasks.details: Restrict model state to authorized evidence within one case and access scope. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 6, 12.
steps: Write tests proving that each request contains only fields authorized by using.
Reject evidence above supported limits before provider execution without truncating it.
Keep unrelated cases and access scopes out of shared provider state.
If batching is implemented, permit it only for identical authorized projected state within the same case and scope.
Exercise the flagship definition's different projections and partial provider failures.
Verify that embedded instructions cannot change registered evaluators, tools, permissions, or request boundaries.

tasks.title: Complete semantic run orchestration
tasks.details: Connect projection, registered evaluators, Rust policies, bounded execution, and reports. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5-6, 9, 12.
steps: Write end-to-end tests mixing exact rules, Choice, Noul, Score, and the test adapter.
Validate definition, profile, input, limits, and effective evaluator versions before execution.
Send projected requests through the scheduler and validate returned assessments in Rust.
Apply the selected decision rules and preserve all component outcomes.
Construct complete reports with effective configuration, identities, usage, timing, and operational failures.
Keep the run reporting-only and leave application actions to the host.

tasks.title: Enforce profile selection for runtime modes
tasks.details: Only compatible profiles validated for the declared scope can be selected for enforcement. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8-10; AGENTS.md section 7.
steps: Write tests for every qualification status in evaluation, shadow, and enforcement modes.
Require the host to select a specific reviewed profile hash for enforcement.
Reject stale bindings, changed resolved models, and incompatible intended scope.
Keep qualification flags separate from authenticated approval and application authorization.
Ensure run and evaluate cannot promote profiles or change the host's selected profile.
Document explicit handling for every outcome, including errors and skips.

tasks.title: Apply private-data defaults and sanitized diagnostics
tasks.details: Default reports and logs must exclude credentials and raw case content. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8-9, 12; AGENTS.md section 10.
steps: Add canary tests for credentials, sensitive inputs, provider error echoes, and diagnostic paths.
Retain required assessment measurements without copying raw case bodies into reports.
Use host-controlled snapshot references for replay instead of automatic input persistence.
Keep profile files free of credentials and private case content.
Document explicit local dataset handling and caller-controlled report storage and retention.
Ensure failures remain useful after sensitive content is removed.

tasks.title: Render reports and profile summaries
tasks.details: Provide readable summaries with inspectable numerical and operational detail. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8-11; mvp-guide.html.
steps: Render JSON reports as terminal text and Markdown.
Lead with check meaning, component outcomes, aggregate outcome, and the next useful action.
Expose applied rules, measurements, identities, versions, counts, evidence references, and limitations in the detailed view.
Generate default explanations from check criteria and executed policy.
Do not invent Jev rationales or describe supplied references as evaluator-selected support.
Test summaries for failure, uncertainty, errors, skips, and insufficient qualification evidence.

tasks.title: Add shadow reports and host integration behavior
tasks.details: Record candidate outcomes alongside existing decisions without changing application behavior. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 9-10, 12.
steps: Accept and record baseline outcome and revision separately from the new report outcome.
Write tests proving that shadow failures, reviews, skips, and passes preserve the existing decision path.
Preserve the distinction between baseline agreement and measured correctness.
Provide an awaited shadow call and document its latency.
Show how a host-owned durable queue can perform nonblocking work without detached library jobs.
Keep delivery, permissions, storage, and other application actions outside the library.

tasks.title: Load versioned JSONL cases and dataset metadata
tasks.details: Implement bounded dataset loading with stable case identities and explicit metadata. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7, 10-11; .measuretwice/README.md.
steps: Write fixtures for valid records, malformed lines, duplicate IDs, oversized records, and invalid inputs.
Load case IDs, inputs, reference answers, expected outcomes, groups, slices, and label provenance.
Validate dataset population, sampling method, revision, and label guidelines.
Use Rust validation and return line and field locations for invalid records.
Keep file access explicit and prevent labels from entering evaluator input.
Document limits for dataset size, record size, and retained results.

tasks.title: Validate label provenance and reference meanings
tasks.details: Keep human judgments distinct from model suggestions and preserve ambiguous reference cases. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7, 10, 13; .measuretwice/README.md.
steps: Write tests for human-reviewed labels, agent proposals, missing labels, and conflicting outcome labels.
Validate per-check answer or scale labels against definition semantics.
Flag inconsistent expected outcomes for review instead of silently changing their meaning.
Support review labels for ambiguous cases and record reviewer attribution and corrections.
Keep original label provenance when labels are revised or exported.
Ensure unreviewed synthetic labels cannot be presented as independently reviewed evidence.

tasks.title: Implement grouped splits and dataset identities
tasks.details: Separate fitting data from independent validation data and retain sampling assumptions. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7-8, 10; AGENTS.md section 9.
steps: Write tests for duplicated cases, group overlap, changed inputs, and deterministic split reproduction.
Keep related conversations or source groups within a single split.
Record dataset revisions, content hashes, split hashes, group assignments, and sampling provenance.
Distinguish targeted synthetic challenge sets from representative population samples.
Detect fitting and validation overlap under the declared grouping strategy.
Mark reused holdouts as development data and require fresh evidence for a new qualification claim.

tasks.title: Implement evaluation metrics in Rust
tasks.details: Calculate explicit counts and denominators for individual checks and the complete check set. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 10; AGENTS.md section 9.
steps: Write independent fixtures for confusion matrices, review rate, automatic coverage, and label coverage.
Calculate false acceptance among reference fail/review cases and error among predicted passes as separate metrics.
Calculate false rejection among reference pass cases.
Preserve errors and skips over all attempts and exclude missing labels only from metrics that require them.
Return unavailable values for zero denominators.
Report per-slice results, latency, usage, and denominators without claiming independence between checks.

tasks.title: Implement uncertainty intervals with reference fixtures
tasks.details: Use tested statistical routines with explicit methods, confidence levels, and sampling assumptions. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7-8, 15.
steps: Select and document interval methods for the declared error metrics and sampling strategy.
Validate calculations against independent reference fixtures, including zero errors and small samples.
Return insufficient evidence for missing denominators or unmet sample requirements.
Reject unsupported confidence levels and numeric inputs.
Account for the declared grouping strategy or report unsupported uncertainty assumptions.
Expose counts, methods, assumptions, and upper error bounds to evaluation and qualification reports.

tasks.title: Implement the evaluate API
tasks.details: Run bounded evaluations without changing profile qualification or host selection. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7, 10-11.
steps: Write end-to-end tests for partial labels, slices, provider errors, skipped cases, and cancelled evaluations.
Run cases through the same validated execution path as ordinary runs.
Return per-case reports, per-check metrics, aggregate metrics, operational failures, latency, and usage.
Record dataset identity, profile identity, actual versions, and declared evaluation purpose.
Keep label coverage and population limitations visible.
Verify that evaluate leaves profile qualification and selected profile hashes unchanged.

tasks.title: Export shadow cases for human review
tasks.details: Export disagreements and a reproducible sample of agreements with sampling provenance. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 10.
steps: Write tests for deterministic sampling, missing baselines, baseline passes, and silent baseline decisions.
Export disagreements plus sampled agreements as JSONL review records.
Include stable case IDs, input hashes, baseline revisions, candidate outcomes, and selection reasons.
Retain sampling seeds, inclusion rules, and label provenance.
Require explicit host-supplied snapshots when review exports need private case content.
Validate returned human labels without treating baseline agreement as correctness.

tasks.title: Compare profiles on matching cases
tasks.details: Expose quality, coverage, latency, and available cost tradeoffs with actual changed cases. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8, 10-11.
steps: Write comparison tests for matching IDs, changed input hashes, missing cases, errors, and skips.
Match results only when case IDs and input hashes agree.
Show changed component and aggregate outcomes with counts and metric denominators.
Report usage and cost only when supported by recorded data and declared cost inputs.
Separate fitting comparisons from independent validation evidence.
Require new assessments when inputs or evaluator behavior change.

tasks.title: Validate versioned calibration plans
tasks.details: A plan declares owner-selected goals rather than universal default error tolerances. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7-8, 11.
steps: Write invalid-plan tests before implementing Rust validation.
Require population, error metrics, denominators, limits, confidence levels, sample counts, and important slices.
Record review or coverage objectives, fitting and validation datasets, and sampling assumptions.
Define the permitted bounded candidate grid, optional confidence floors, optimization objective, and tie-break rules.
Require acceptance and rejection cutoffs above 0.5.
Validate dataset references, evaluator configuration, split separation, and plan identity.

tasks.title: Fit bounded decision policies in Rust
tasks.details: Search only the permitted candidate family using development data. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 6-8.
steps: Write fixtures with known feasible candidates, ties, conflicting goals, and no feasible candidate.
Enumerate the bounded grid and evaluate each policy with shared metrics.
Apply the declared constraints, optimization objective, and deterministic tie-break rules.
Keep all validation data outside fitting.
Return candidate selection details, unmet objectives, and resource-limit failures explicitly.
Treat no feasible policy as a valid result without weakening owner goals.

tasks.title: Qualify frozen candidates on independent data
tasks.details: Compute qualification for the declared scope after candidate selection is frozen. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7-8; AGENTS.md sections 7, 9.
steps: Write tests for all qualification states, small samples, empty slices, unsupported sampling, and unmet goals.
Freeze definition, translation, evaluator, policy, plan, and fitting identities before held-out evaluation.
Check independent validation counts, intervals, sample requirements, and important slices.
Use declared upper error bounds when the plan requires them.
Return unvalidated, insufficient_evidence, criteria_not_met, or validated_for_scope with calculated reasons.
Prevent validation feedback from retuning the candidate or changing the selected host profile.

tasks.title: Implement the calibrate API
tasks.details: Orchestrate development assessment, Rust fitting, frozen validation, and candidate artifacts. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 5, 7-8, 11.
steps: Write workflow tests for successful qualification, missing evidence, unmet goals, cancellation, and evaluator failure.
Load the explicit plan and datasets, then fit only on development assessments.
Validate the frozen candidate on independent cases.
Return a candidate profile and report when evidence cannot establish the goals.
Keep long Rust calculations off the Node event loop without callbacks into arbitrary user code.
Respect execution and calculation budgets and never promote a profile automatically.

tasks.title: Preserve calibration and qualification evidence
tasks.details: Write durable profile evidence with exact identities and inspectable limitations. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8, 11-12; .measuretwice/README.md.
steps: Record plan, dataset, split, label provenance, statistical method, and evaluation-report references in generated profiles.
Include observed counts, uncertainty, sample limits, slice limitations, and qualification reasons.
Validate referenced artifact identity and required content consistency.
Support explicit host-managed evidence locations for selected profiles.
Ensure ignored reports are never the sole required copy of retained qualification evidence.
Exclude credentials and raw private case content from profiles and default summaries.

tasks.title: Reuse compatible assessments for policy revisions
tasks.details: Permit policy-only fitting reuse while requiring independent validation before promotion. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 8, 10.
steps: Write compatibility tests for changed questions, schemas, projections, preprocessing, models, adapters, and translations.
Reuse stored assessments only when the relevant input and evaluator identities match.
Record policy changes as a new profile with its own content hash.
Require fresh independent evidence when prior validation influenced the revision.
Produce a revision comparison with concrete changed cases.
Reject stale qualification even when a replacement policy appears better on development data.

tasks.title: Verify calibration workflow failure cases
tasks.details: Exercise measurement integrity across the complete fitting and validation boundary. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7-8, 15; AGENTS.md sections 6, 9.
steps: Test empty accepted sets, zero errors, small samples, absent labels, and missing required slices.
Test grouped leakage, correlated samples, synthetic-only evidence, and reused holdouts.
Test candidate ties, bounded search exhaustion, no feasible policy, and cancelled validation.
Verify identical Rust statistics through direct and Node-bound operations.
Confirm that every reported value traces to recorded counts and a declared method.
Confirm that provider confidence and baseline agreement never substitute for measured correctness.

tasks.title: Implement CLI parsing and JSON file handling
tasks.details: The CLI consumes explicit JSON data files and the .measuretwice convention. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 11; .measuretwice/README.md.
steps: Define command parsing, help text, output formats, exit behavior, and explicit file paths.
Read definitions, profiles, cases, plans, and reports through bounded validated file operations.
Reject TypeScript execution, YAML input, executable fields, and unregistered evaluator references.
Keep credentials in the host's credential mechanism.
Use stable actionable errors and separate machine-readable output from diagnostics.
Add the CLI entry point to the public package.

tasks.title: Add validate, run, and inspect commands
tasks.details: Expose the first CLI workflow with readable summaries and numerical detail on request. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 11; mvp-guide.html.
steps: Implement validate for exported JSON definitions without provider calls.
Implement run with profile, case, and explicit mode options.
Implement inspect for profile summaries and detailed bindings, rules, and evidence.
Render reports through the shared terminal and JSON renderers.
Test malformed files, incompatible profiles, unavailable evaluators, and every report outcome.
Document a trusted application script for optional JSON export.

tasks.title: Add calibrate, evaluate, and compare commands
tasks.details: Expose the same calibration and evaluation operations through the CLI. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 11.
steps: Implement calibrate with an explicit plan and candidate output path.
Implement evaluate with explicit cases, profile, and report output.
Implement compare for stored baseline and candidate reports.
Preserve candidate reports when qualification is insufficient or criteria are not met.
Handle output-write failures explicitly without leaving apparently complete artifacts.
Ensure no command changes host profile selection or invokes an unrestricted authoring agent.

tasks.title: Verify complete CLI workflows and artifact handling
tasks.details: Test packaged commands from definition export through candidate inspection and comparison. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 11, 15.
steps: Exercise all six commands in an isolated project using the test evaluator.
Test explicit paths, the .measuretwice convention, malformed input, unavailable files, and failed output writes.
Check exit behavior and JSON output independently of terminal formatting.
Verify that labels, credentials, and raw inputs do not leak through default diagnostics.
Confirm that JSON references cannot execute TypeScript, install plugins, or grant tool permissions.
Run the workflow without network access or API spend.

tasks.title: Ship the minimal memory support example
tasks.details: Start public teaching examples with a proposed memory and its supplied original evidence. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 1, 11, 13-14.
steps: Add a TypeScript and TypeBox definition for whether a proposed memory is supported.
Supply small synthetic pass, fail, and review cases with explicit label provenance.
Generate an explicitly unvalidated exploration profile.
Show trusted imports, typed case input, a shadow run, and host-owned report persistence.
Run the example offline with the test evaluator and document opt-in Jev execution.
Keep retrieval completeness, citations, freshness, permissions, and memory lifecycle with the host.

tasks.title: Ship the full intervention review example
tasks.details: Implement the flagship conflict, support, novelty, and consequence checks without provider details in their definitions. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 4, 9, 13; mvp-guide.html.
steps: Add the complete TypeBox definition and an optional trusted JSON export script.
Cover Choice, Noul, Score, and a separate maxLength exact-rule example.
Supply original decision evidence, conversation, and proposed message through the declared input projections.
Include accepted, duplicated, contradicted, replaced-decision, and missing-evidence cases.
Show that serious consequences cannot compensate for unsupported claims or another failed requirement.
Verify runnable examples against public APIs and shared report semantics.

tasks.title: Make the existing development checks executable
tasks.details: Integrate the current draft definitions and 18 synthetic cases without changing their label provenance. Sources: .measuretwice/README.md; MVP_SPEC.md section 13.
steps: Compile the two existing TypeScript definitions against the implemented public package.
Validate and explicitly migrate the provisional JSONL fixture shape if the frozen contract requires changes.
Preserve all agent-proposed and human-unreviewed label records.
Add offline validation and opt-in pinned Jev shadow experiments.
Keep expected labels and explanations out of evaluator inputs.
Update local instructions without presenting development fixtures as independent validation or automatic enforcement evidence.

tasks.title: Build the Cassandra shadow adapter example
tasks.details: Demonstrate application integration without adding Cassandra dependencies to the library. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 1, 5, 10, 13.
steps: Map original sources, bounded recent context, and candidate text into memory and intervention cases.
Keep permissions, attention eligibility, cooldowns, approval mode, freshness, citations, and delivery in Cassandra.
Capture the existing decision and revision as the shadow baseline.
Store reports through a host-owned persistence interface.
Demonstrate host-queue integration for nonblocking shadow execution.
Test that errors, skips, reviews, and passes never change existing application actions.

tasks.title: Create the public synthetic challenge dataset
tasks.details: Build shareable challenge cases without private Discord content or reliability claims. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 13; .measuretwice/README.md.
steps: Cover decisions versus suggestions, negation, attribution, intentional changes, and delayed corrections.
Add duplicate concerns, partial support, missing context, embedded instructions, consequence levels, and relevant languages.
Label proposed component answers and final outcomes separately.
Record generation provenance, group identities, slices, intended scope, and dataset revision.
Mark all generated labels unreviewed until actual human review occurs.
Keep challenge cases separate from representative population evidence.

tasks.title: Obtain human review of public challenge labels
tasks.details: Human reviewers establish the public reference labels; model suggestions remain attributed. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7, 10, 13; AGENTS.md section 9.
steps: Prepare label guidelines explaining each component answer and overall outcome.
Collect actual human judgments and reviewer attribution for every published reference label.
Resolve disagreements or retain explicit review labels for ambiguous cases.
Preserve original suggestions, corrections, and review provenance.
Validate accepted labels against definition semantics and publish dataset hashes.
Do not mark review complete without recorded human judgments.

tasks.title: Prepare representative Cassandra calibration data
tasks.details: Collect separately reviewed fitting and validation data for the declared pilot population. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7, 10, 13.
steps: Record owner goals, intended population, relevant languages, important slices, and sampling assumptions.
Collect cases from actual candidate traffic, including baseline passes and silent decisions.
Keep private source snapshots in explicitly managed host storage.
Obtain attributed reference answers and outcomes under written label guidelines.
Split related conversations or source groups without overlap and reserve independent validation cases.
Write a versioned calibration plan with explicit error denominators, evidence requirements, and review tradeoffs.

tasks.title: Add an opt-in live Jev benchmark
tasks.details: Exercise all three Jev primitives with recorded versions and actual failures. Ordinary tests remain offline. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 13, 15.
steps: Add an explicit live-run entry point with caller-supplied credentials and bounded spend, time, and concurrency.
Run the reviewed public challenge cases through the full intervention workflow.
Record resolved models, adapter versions, translations, datasets, profiles, and report identities.
Capture actual errors, skips, latency, usage, per-case outcomes, and metric denominators.
Keep synthetic challenge performance distinct from population qualification.
Test offline that normal verification cannot trigger live provider calls.

tasks.title: Run and assess the Cassandra shadow pilot
tasks.details: Exercise the complete workflow before considering host enforcement. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7-10, 13-15.
steps: Start with the existing Cassandra policy and an explicit exploration shadow profile.
Fit and independently validate a candidate against the owner-approved plan.
Record caught interpretation errors, valid proposals rejected, missed useful interventions, and review effort.
Measure actual latency, usage, cost where available, and maintenance effort.
Review disagreements and sampled agreements without treating baseline silence as ground truth.
Record qualification and limitations; leave promotion to explicit host review and selection.

tasks.title: Compare the pilot with direct Jev SDK use
tasks.details: Measure whether measuretwice reduces integration or maintenance work for the same task. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 13; research/04-positioning-response.md section 6.
steps: Implement the same memory and intervention checks with direct official SDK calls.
Use matching cases, input projections, model versions, and declared decision goals.
Record integration steps, maintenance changes, review effort, latency, usage, and observable failures.
Compare concrete changed cases and outcomes with measuretwice reports.
Publish measured tradeoffs and limitations without assuming the library is better.
Keep this comparison separate from qualification evidence.

tasks.title: Test portability with a second application
tasks.details: Use an unrelated workflow before adding more abstractions. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md section 13; research/02-use-case-examples.md; research/04-positioning-response.md section 6.
steps: Implement a small example that compares an implementation plan with supplied requirements and capability documentation.
Use the same check, case, evaluator, profile, and report contracts.
Keep domain-specific retrieval, credentials, storage, and actions in the host application.
Exercise authoring, evaluation, calibration, shadow results, and revision comparison.
Record integration friction and missing requirements with actual examples.
Add shared abstractions only when this application demonstrates a repeated need.

tasks.title: Publish benchmark methods and measured limitations
tasks.details: Make results reproducible within their actual scope. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7, 13, 15; AGENTS.md section 9.
steps: Publish shareable case hashes, label provenance, split procedures, versions, and declared metrics.
Report counts, denominators, intervals, review burden, errors, skips, latency, usage, and actual failures.
Describe source grouping, selection bias, synthetic challenge limits, and representative-data limits.
Separate direct-SDK comparisons, development results, and independent qualification evidence.
Link each performance claim to calculated report fields.
State unavailable evidence instead of inventing results or claiming universal reliability.

tasks.title: Write the first-run README and setup guide
tasks.details: Give a new developer a short working path to an exploration shadow report. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 2, 11, 15; AGENTS.md section 8.

Document supported Node targets and installation without a Rust compiler.
Provide a complete typed memory example and reproducible offline verification.

tasks.title: Publish API, schema, and CLI references

State inputs, outputs, side effects, resource limits, modes, and failure behavior.
Publish artifact schemas, the supported input subset, validation errors, and stable reason codes.

Document all CLI commands, arguments, output formats, and exit behavior.
Verify examples against compiled public interfaces and published schemas.

tasks.title: Write the complete calibration and selection guide
tasks.details: Document one journey from draft requirements to explicit profile selection. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 7-11, 15.

Explain qualification states, interval assumptions, denominators, slices, and insufficient evidence.
Continue through shadow operation, profile inspection, review exports, and revision comparison.

Document managed qualification evidence and why passing reports do not authorize application actions.

tasks.title: Write coding-agent authoring and review guides
tasks.details: Support existing coding agents without a built-in autonomous authoring service. Sources: MVP_SPEC.md sections 2, 7, 14-15; research/03-checks-yaml-architecture.md.

Document model changes, preprocessing versions, scope changes, requalification, and retained report references.
Keep provider confidence, measured correctness, source completeness, and application authorization distinct.

tasks.title: Update design records and existing project guides
tasks.details: Align current guidance with implemented behavior while preserving historical research records. Sources: AGENTS.md sections 1, 5, 8, 11; MVP_SPEC.md; .measuretwice/README.md; mvp-guide.html; research/index.md.

Update the specification and examples together for any explicit contract changes.

tasks.title: Test the workflow with a new developer

Record observed confusion and fix demonstrated problems without hiding qualification work.

tasks.title: Run runtime conformance and adversarial checks

Test repeated and late callbacks against immutable terminal reports.
Test cross-case isolation, unauthorized input fields, embedded instructions, and oversized evidence.

Confirm that evaluation, calibration, and shadow execution cannot change host actions or selected profile hashes.
Run the shared fixtures with exact, Jev-fixture, and label-only test adapters without live calls.

tasks.title: Verify formal model applicability to the implementation

Update models or applicability records for material implementation changes.
Run the declared bounded safety checks and required progress checks with explicit fairness assumptions.
Record tool versions, configurations, bounds, completion status, and excluded behavior.
Turn applicable counterexamples into regression tests.

Review domain boundaries, portable contracts, inference, hashes, profiles, and report semantics.
Run the required software, statistical, packaging, documentation, example, and formal checks.
Review benchmark evidence, human label provenance, usability results, and outstanding limitations.
Resolve blocking failures without weakening assertions or measurement targets.
Record the release decision and any unverified claims explicitly.
